chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail al-Khash'i, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When we arrive in Mecca, our companions go to perform Tawaf and leave me to guard their belongings.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'You are greater than them in reward.'

key_terms.يَطُوفُونَ: They perform Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for guarding belongings while others perform Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the act of *hafz* (guarding belongings) during Hajj from a mere logistical necessity to a superior act of worship (*ibadah*), illustrating the Shia principle that sincere service to others can outweigh personal ritual devotion. This reflects the broader scholarly emphasis on *khidmah* (service) and *amanah* (trustworthiness) as integral components of spiritual merit, where the intent and sacrifice of the guardian are valued highly by the Imam.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ismail Al Khash’amy who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘When we arrived in Makkah, our companions went to perform Tawaaf, and left me to guard their provisions’. Heasws said: ‘You are greater than them in Recompense’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Isma‘il af-Khath’amiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘When we arrived in Makkah, our people went for Tawaf and left me to look after their belongings . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Your reward is the greatest among them.’”
